subject.title: fix(azure): responses model aliases route correctly

question: Should this PR land with resolver-layer mock Azure Responses proof, or should maintainers require a live Azure credential exchange before merging the auth-provider routing change?
rationale: The patch looks correct at the resolver boundary, but it changes auth-provider ownership for existing Azure Responses routes and live Azure credentials were not exercised.

options.title: Accept resolver-layer proof
options.body: Merge after exact-head CI refresh if maintainers agree the local mock Responses probe proves the OpenClaw routing bug without needing live Azure credentials.

options.title: Require live Azure smoke
options.body: Ask for a redacted live Azure Responses probe or agent run before merge to prove credential exchange against the real service.

options.title: Pause for owner-boundary redesign
options.body: Hold the PR only if maintainers want a broader provider/alias ownership model instead of this targeted resolver fix.

recommendation.title: Accept resolver-layer proof
recommendation.body: Merge after exact-head CI refresh if maintainers agree the local mock Responses probe proves the OpenClaw routing bug without needing live Azure credentials.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent OpenAI/model-catalog ownership history makes this the best available owner for the proof and routing-boundary decision.
